literacy_definition: A person who can both read and write a simple message with understanding in at least one language was considered as literate for the purpose of the survey.
method: Stratified multistage probability household sample survey. Annual detailed tables use first-visit schedules in rural and urban areas. The revamped design from January 2025 uses a four-consecutive-month rotational panel in both sectors, 12 sampled households per selected FSU, updated Census 2011 village/sub-unit rural frame and latest Urban Frame Survey block/sub-unit urban frame. Rates are weighted ratios of estimated aggregates, not arithmetic averages of states or sectors.

sample_all_ages.note: All-age sample counts, not the age-7-plus denominator or definitive population counts.
sample_all_ages.reference: Chapter 1, Table 3, printed page 7 / PDF page 37; Table (1), printed A-1 and A-2 / PDF pages 78 and 79.

coverage: Whole Indian Union except villages in Andaman and Nicobar Islands that remained extremely difficult to access throughout the year; report Highlights printed xii / PDF page 17.
missing_or_suppressed: No missing or suppressed overall/male/female cells in the 36 rural-plus-urban rows.
Rural Chandigarh is blank. Appendix A note on PDF page 77: For Chandigarh as per the frame there is no rural area. Stored as null, not zero, and not backfilled.

Chapter 1 section 1.7.3, PDF page 38: percentages exclude not-reported cases. A displayed zero elsewhere can mean no sample observation or a value below 0.05; none of the selected numeric literacy cells is zero.
gender_note: Persons includes transgender respondents; male and female are separate categories. There were 37 transgender persons in the full all-age sample; for 2025 they are included only in persons. Chapter 1 sections 1.6.1.3 and 1.7.3 / PDF pages 37-38.
comparability_limits: The 2025 sampling design and estimation procedure differ from earlier PLFS. Annual 2025 estimates may not be strictly comparable with earlier annual reports or 2022-2024 calendar-year results. PDF page 38 / printed page 8.
Survey point estimates of household-reported literacy status, not a Census, direct achievement tests, numeracy, school enrolment, or completion rates.
Appendix B publishes RSEs for LFPR, WPR and unemployment, not literacy. Small-area rankings are descriptive, not verified statistically significant differences. PDF page 527.
Rates are rounded to one decimal. Gaps are percentage points calculated from those rounded rates.
No historical geography backfills or mixing with Census 2011, NSS 2017-18, CAMS 2022-23 or literacy declarations.
